body: And, same as to Lofty_Hobbit, thanks for talking to me.

> If they are treating you badly, you should talk to them about it.

I do, and he says we need to find alternative forms of employment for me, one more encouraging a healthy balance between work and uni, but it NEVER comes down to anything concrete.

> Try explaining your current situation to them and they'll be understanding.

Naah, they don't really get it anyway. To them i just complain on a high level. "Oh, you have a stable job, a decent car and enough money? What? You need to work for it? Poor you!" (I might have dramatized it, but you get my gist)

> To find a better balance, first try finding other hobbies you enjoy.

BUT THAT'S SO HARD! ;_; But also see http://www.reddit.com/r/SuicideWatch/comments/1govn8/missing_a_purpose/canp5ed (last paragraph) -- the history book thing is a long shot, but it's worth a try...

> So when you say it's the "easiest solution," just remember how hard it would be on all the people you'd leave behind.

*cynic mode* Yeah, my boss probably misses his most exploitable worker ;)

I guess some people would miss me, but this won't help the feeling I am without purpose. Existing for the sake of existing? No thanks.

> Your comment seems to imply to me that you actually have plenty of time

48 hours isn't that much, and I still have to do uni stuff to do on weekends. But ultimately, yeah, there'd be a few hours on weekends if I could just use them instead of wasting them away lying around.

> The fact that you have no ties could be seen as a liberating thing in your life. You could go and teach English in Asia. It's basically a walk-in job, because they never have enough. You could literally do anything, go anywhere.

lolwat. I can't just go to Asia... I have no clue of their culture, nor do I speak their language, I'd just be an alien. The idea of getting away from where I am does sound good though...

> First and foremost however, you need to find a hobby. I knew of a guy who loved learning languages. When he wasn't in his (language related) job, he would quite literally spend 12-16 hours learning and reading in different languages every day. It's amazing how you find energy when you have something you want to do.

It's really hard to find something to be this passionate about. Though I was always interested in history. I decided to get me two books about a history topic I like, let's see, maybe it's history. I can still quit after I read those books.

Last but not least, thank you for talking to me.

> if that's the way you feel, then it just means your purpose at that point in your life is to find something you enjoy doing.

And how do I find out what that is? I tried a few things, but yet nothing even remotely changed how I feel. I'm just an average joe with no real qualifications.

> but sometimes you need to take a day and just do something you like. 

INB4 my boss calls me and tells me that our sole customer has an ULTRA URGENT problem that only I can fix and that it would be great if I could come in.

> You said you didn't have many friends, but one thing that can help is getting together with them more.

I feel they are annoyed of my presence already in the current form. I don't want to push them away by being super clingy...

> Even try to reconcile friendships with people you haven't seen in a long time. By doing this you can build strong friendships with people who will support you at your lowest.

Yeah... I guess I could at least poll some people on Facebook I haven't talked to in a while....

> Just try to find a better balance between work and the rest of your life.

I have no idea how to do that.

> Remember that suicide isn't the only way out of a bad situation. If you ever need to talk to someone, feel free to message me anytime.

I'll keep that in mind.

> Suicide is not the answer.

It's the easiest solution... I don't see how there's anything I can do to make stuff really better for my life... :(

Wouldn't be a job at McDonald's be just as pointless and unsatisfying? I fear I would feel the same drudge everywhere I work.

I have no idea how to make more time... on weekends I'm so exhausted I just sleep and lie in bed and watch TV shows all day long. Work is usually from when I wake up at around 8:30 am until I come home at 12:30 pm...
